description: Results from the literature that bear on this repository's numbers and verdicts, each read from its primary source. A person adds entries; nothing here is ingested automatically. Every claim names the setting it holds in, one kind of evidence and what it does not establish, so the qualifiers travel with the number. Schema: frontier_results.schema.json. Guard: tooling/test_frontier_results.py. Evidence values: .github/skills/scientific-claims/SKILL.md.

claims.statement: In seven of the eight tasks, the discovered circuits significantly reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts relative to the state of the art.

G_TQ is the baseline TQ-cost divided by the discovered TQ-cost; where a baseline has free parameters they are chosen to minimise its TQ-cost

citation.title: How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers with less than a million noisy qubits

claims.statement: I estimate that a 2048 bit RSA integer could be factored in less than a week by a quantum computer with less than a million noisy qubits.
conditions: A square grid of qubits with nearest-neighbour connections
A uniform gate error rate of 0.1%
A surface code cycle time of 1 microsecond and a control system reaction time of 10 microseconds
The reduction comes mainly from approximate residue arithmetic, yoked surface codes for idle logical qubits, and allocating less space to magic state distillation by using magic state cultivation
does_not_establish: Execution on quantum hardware
A logical-qubit count: the abstract gives none, so read the body before quoting one

qualifiers: 0.1% uniform gate error, 1 microsecond cycle, 10 microsecond reaction time, square grid
Under the same assumptions

claims.statement: For 2048-bit RSA integers, Table 5 gives 6.5e9 expected Toffoli gates per factoring and 1,399 logical qubits.
claims.location: Section 3.1, Table 5, n = 2048 row; Section 3.2 for the peak and layout counts
conditions: Logical costs of the paper's variant of the Chevignard-Fouque-Schrottenloher algorithm, which uses approximate residue arithmetic, with the Table 5 parameters for n = 2048 (s = 8, l = 21, f = 33, m = 1280)
The Toffoli column counts expected Toffolis per factoring, not per shot; the expected number of shots is 9.2
Section 3.2 counts 1,409 logical qubits active at the peak, during loop4, and 1,537 including idle hot patches, which the layout keeps below 1,600

citation.title: Approximate sampling from decoded quantum interferometry via Markov chain Monte Carlo methods

claims.statement: In OPI, in the regime where a super-polynomial advantage is claimed for DQI, we observe an empirical runtime for MCMC that scales approximately as 1.1^n, indicating exponential growth with a comparatively small base. Our findings do not refute existing quantum advantage claims but provide new empirical evidence that classical sampling algorithms can closely match DQI's optimization performance.
conditions: Classical Markov chain Monte Carlo, chiefly block-Gibbs sampling, from the ideal DQI output distribution, whose probabilities can be computed efficiently
OPI instances beyond 150 effective qubits, and max-XORSAT beyond 1000
The runtime scaling is fitted to the sizes run; n is the problem size as the paper defines it, which this entry did not check beyond the abstract
does_not_establish: A polynomial-time classical algorithm for OPI
That DQI's claimed superpolynomial speedup is false; the authors say their findings do not refute it
